info.title: FlyItalyADSB API
info.summary: Live and historical aircraft positions worldwide from the FlyItalyADSB community ADS-B/MLAT network. Commercial use allowed on every plan, Free included; the whole world in one request from the Pro plan (€49/month).
info.description: Unfiltered aircraft data (no FAA/LADD/BARR filtering; military aircraft included, many of them via MLAT) from a global network of receivers run by volunteers (about 3,200 receivers, densest in North America and Europe; any point on Earth can be queried), as readsb aircraft.json records (the same format as tar1090), plus an ADS-B Exchange v2–compatible variant at /api/aircraft/v2. PIA and LADD aircraft are flagged in the dbFlags bit field (value 4 for PIA, 8 for LADD), so your product can hide them where its market or app store requires. Every endpoint except the key signup needs an X-Api-Key; keys are self-serve (see /auth.md). Plans and limits: https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/#piani. The same key works on the MCP server at https://flyitalyadsb.com/mcp. The same data is also served in the ADS-B Exchange v2 format (same paths, key headers and JSON; radius in nautical miles) at https://api.flyitalyadsb.com/api/aircraft/v2, documented at https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/adsbx-v2/. Operated by Nesso Labs S.r.l. (ISO/IEC 27001:2022, QMSCERT 160426-7).

tags.name: live
tags.description: What the network is receiving now.

tags.name: history
tags.description: Tracks: per-aircraft daily tracks, every day since 2023-03-03 except 2026-05-05 and 2026-05-06, and the first and last point of each flight from 2022-04-10; and the aircraft that flew over a place (since 2026-08-17).

tags.name: flights
tags.description: Flight history: the flights the network saw (departure and arrival airport, times, duration), built every night from its own tracks since 2026-10-23; yesterday and earlier; not airline schedules. How far back depends on the plan. On Fleet the aircraft and callsign answers also carry today's flights, from takeoffs and landings detected in real time. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#observed-flights

tags.description: The key's account: the position saved for "aircraft near me".

get.summary: One aircraft by ICAO address
get.description: Up to 50 comma-separated values (one comma is enough, at the end too) return a list instead, counted as ONE request: `{now, count, total, ac, not_found, matched}`, each value with the same tolerant forms; then `fields` and `with` apply. Without a comma, the single aircraft or the explained 404. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#several-aircraft-in-one-request

parameters.name: hex
parameters.description: 24-bit ICAO address, hex (case-insensitive, an 0x prefix is accepted). Or up to 50 of them, comma-separated.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Only these fields of each aircraft, comma-separated. `light` = hex, flight, r, t, lat, lon, alt_baro, gs, track, squawk, seen_pos, category (a fixed list). Presets and names can be mixed (`light,rssi`). `hex` is always present and first; a field the aircraft does not have is missing, as in the full record. An unknown name: 400 with `allowed` and `presets`, not counted. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#list-options

parameters.name: with
parameters.description: `route` adds `route` to each aircraft whose callsign has a known route: the most frequent one in the latest 7 days of flight history (not a schedule). The field is absent when no route is known. Any other value: 400, not counted.

200.description: One value: the aircraft currently seen with this identifier, unchanged; X-Matched-As and X-Matched-Value are present when it was found under another form of the identifier. Comma-separated values: the aircraft in the air now, with `not_found` and `matched`.

400.description: More than 50 comma-separated values, or none, or an invalid list option; not counted.

404.description: No aircraft with this identifier is in the air and seen by the network right now. The body says what was tried, a hint, `found_as` when the text is another identifier of an airborne aircraft, and `last_seen`, the last observed flight, when there is one.

get.summary: All aircraft in a latitude/longitude box
get.description: Edges included. lon_west greater than lon_east crosses the antimeridian (170/-170 = from 170 E to 170 W). The plan's maximum radius applies to the half-diagonal, the great-circle distance from the centre of the box to its farthest point; above it, the same 403 as the radius. One request. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#aircraft-in-a-box

parameters.name: lon_east
parameters.description: Eastern edge, decimal degrees; different from lon_west.

get.summary: The runway an airport is using now (estimate)
get.description: Estimated from the aircraft the network sees now within 25 km of the airport: an aircraft counts for a runway end when it is below 5,000 ft above the field, lined up within 20 degrees and within 1 km of the extended centreline, and either arriving (not climbing, up to 18 km before the threshold), departing (climbing, over the runway or up to 12 km after it) or rolling on it at 40 kt or more; with parallel runways the nearest centreline wins. An estimate, not an official source: a quiet airport can show no runway (empty in_use). Runways from OurAirports (public domain), refreshed nightly. One request. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#runway-in-use

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Airport ICAO (e.g. LIMC) or IATA (e.g. MXP) code.

200.description: The runways in use now, busiest first. Cacheable for 15 seconds.

404.description: Unknown airport code ("unknown airport code"), or no runway data for this airport ("no runway data for this airport").

503.description: The runway data is not loaded yet ("runway data is not available yet"), or live data is briefly unavailable: retry later.

get.summary: Dates with a recorded track for one aircraft

parameters.name: icao
parameters.description: 24-bit ICAO address, 6 hex characters.

400.description: icao is not 6 hex characters.

get.summary: One aircraft's track for one day
get.description: readsb's trace_full file for that aircraft and day, passed through as written. From 2022-04-10 to 2023-10-04 the archive also holds imported Virtual Radar Server data: only the first and last point of each flight ("version": "vrs-basestation-import"). From 2023-03-03 that file is returned only when there is no full track for that aircraft and day. The current day is built from readsb's live trace files (X-History-Source live), or from the overflights store once readsb no longer has the aircraft (store: position, altitude, flags, source and callsign only); it may answer 503 while a file is being written. With since, only the points after that time, the rest of the file unchanged (X-Since-Applied: 1). https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#since

parameters.name: icao
parameters.description: 24-bit ICAO address, 6 hex characters.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Unix time in seconds: keep only the points with timestamp + offset > since. Milliseconds, negative or non-numeric values: 400, not counted. Empty = absent.

X-History-Source.description: Where the day was read from: `local` (the server), `r2` (the archive), `live` (today, readsb's live trace) or `store` (today, the overflights store).

400.description: icao or date is malformed, the date is in the future, or since is not a Unix time in seconds.

404.description: No trace for this aircraft on this date.

502.description: The archived trace could not be read.

503.description: The archive is briefly unavailable, or today's file is being written: retry shortly.

get.summary: Profile of one aircraft
get.description: Identity (registration, ICAO type, type description, year, decoded dbFlags), live status (position, callsign and position source when received now) and a history summary (first and last day with a track, days in the last 30 UTC days, total days; the same dates as /v2/history/{icao}), plus links to the public map and to a public photo page. One request. Never returns owner or operator names. No photo is embedded: Planespotters.net's API terms forbid re-serving their photos through another API, so `photos.page` is a link to their public page, and it is null (with `withheld`) for PIA and LADD aircraft.

parameters.name: icao
parameters.description: 24-bit ICAO address, 6 hex characters.

400.description: icao is not 6 hex characters.

404.description: Not received now and no recorded history for this aircraft.

503.description: Live data or the archive is briefly unavailable: retry shortly.

get.summary: Aircraft that flew over a place in a time window
get.description: Every aircraft whose recorded track passed within `dist` km of the point between `from` and `to`, one entry per aircraft, sorted by the time of its closest point. Tracks are interpolated between received positions (gaps over 5 minutes are not). Covers the days since 2026-08-17, the current day up to about 10 minutes ago, and the periods not searched are listed in `coverage.gaps`. One request per call. The maximum `dist` and window depend on the plan (Free 10 km / 6 h, Starter 25 km / 24 h, others 50 km / 24 h): https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/#piani. Aircraft data only: registration, type, description and dbFlags, never the owner or operator.

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude, decimal degrees.

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude, decimal degrees.

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: Radius in km.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start: ISO 8601 (UTC when there is no offset) or Unix seconds.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End, after `from`: ISO 8601 or Unix seconds. A time in the future is cut to now.

parameters.name: max_alt_ft
parameters.description: Only the part of each track at or below this altitude (feet); positions without altitude are left out.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many aircraft.

200.description: The overflights, with what was searched.

400.description: A parameter is missing or malformed, `to` is not after `from`, or the circle contains a pole.

403.description: `dist` or the window is above the plan's maximum (the body carries max_dist_km and max_window_hours).

503.description: Too many searches at once, or the index is briefly unavailable: retry shortly (Retry-After).

get.summary: Flight history of a callsign, and its usual routes
get.description: The flights of a callsign the network observed in the last days, newest first, and its usual routes (`usual`, with how many times each was flown). The callsign takes the same forms as /v2/callsign, so a flight number works too (matched_as/matched_value say which form matched). A callsign with no flights answers 200 with count 0. How far back `days` can go depends on the plan: https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#observed-flights-depth. On Fleet the JSON answer also carries `today`: the flights since `since` (today, UTC), from takeoffs and landings detected in real time, with an estimated arrival time for an aircraft in flight; on other plans `today` is {available: false, error, plans}. These answers are cached privately for at most 15 seconds. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#todays-flights

parameters.name: callsign
parameters.description: Callsign or flight number.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days back, up to yesterday.

200.description: The callsign's flight history: the flights the network saw.

400.description: A parameter is malformed or out of range.

503.description: The flights index is briefly unavailable: retry shortly.

get.summary: Flight history of one aircraft (flight log)
get.description: One aircraft's flight history (the flights the network saw) between two UTC days (default the last 7 available days, at most 31 per request), newest first, with a summary (flights, minutes, airports) for flight hours. An aircraft with no flights in the period answers 200 with count 0. `format=csv` returns the same flights as a CSV flight log (text/csv), one row per flight, oldest first. How far back `from` can go depends on the plan (403 code flights-depth beyond it, not counted): https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#observed-flights-depth. On Fleet the JSON answer also carries `today`: the flights since `since` (today, UTC), from takeoffs and landings detected in real time, with an estimated arrival time for an aircraft in flight; on other plans `today` is {available: false, error, plans}. These answers are cached privately for at most 15 seconds. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/endpoints/#todays-flights

parameters.name: hex

On Fleet the JSON answer also carries `today`: the flights since `since` (today, UTC), from takeoffs and landings detected in real time, with an estimated arrival time for an aircraft in flight; on other plans `today` is {available: false, error, plans}. One event per aircraft, kind and ~0.5° grid cell it entered, so a long flight appears once per cell; a new event for the same cell only after 30 (emergency) or 60 minutes away. Newest first. Counted as one request; the plan's radius applies. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/alerts/

An area webhook has lat, lon and dist (capped by the plan's radius) and area kinds. A webhook for the watched aircraft (Fleet) has kinds takeoff and/or landing and no area: it receives flight.takeoff, flight.landing and flight.landing_retracted for every aircraft in /v2/watch. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/alerts/#aircraft

post.summary: Request an API key by email
post.description: Sends a one-time link (valid 7 days) to the address; opening it shows the key once. The key is never in this response or in the email. Requesting again for the same address rotates the self-serve key when the new link is used; until then the old key keeps working. One free key per mailbox (+tag and Gmail-dot variants count as the same mailbox); temporary email domains are refused.

found_via.description: Required. How you found FlyItalyADSB. An agent signing up for its user sends the assistant it is (e.g. claude, chatgpt); the official Python client sends pypi.

audience.description: Who the data is for. Accepted now and will become required: agents should send it already (ask the user rather than guess). Unknown value: 400, code "audience-invalid", with "allowed".

other_source.description: Whether another flight data source is already in use and what role this one will have: none (this is the first), switching (it becomes the main one), backup, comparing. Accepted now and will become required: agents should send it already. Unknown value: 400, code "other-source-invalid", with "allowed".

other_source_name.description: With other_source other than "none": which source.

ai_prompt.description: Optional, kept only when found_via is an AI assistant (chatgpt, claude, perplexity, gemini, copilot, other_ai): what the user asked it.

options_order.description: Site form only: the order in which the form showed the options.

400.description: Missing or invalid email, a temporary email domain (code "disposable-email"), a missing or unknown found_via (code "found-via-required", with the accepted codes in "allowed"), an unknown audience or other_source (codes "audience-invalid", "other-source-invalid"; once they are required, "audience-required", "other-source-required"), or invalid JSON.

post.summary: A notable-traffic event, sent to your webhook URL
post.description: Signed with Standard Webhooks (https://www.standardwebhooks.com/): HMAC-SHA256 with the base64-decoded part of the secret after "whsec_", over "{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}". Reject a timestamp more than 5 minutes away and dedupe on webhook-id, which is the same on every retry. Answer 2xx within 10 seconds; anything else (redirects included) is retried 6 times over about 5 hours. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/alerts/

post.summary: A takeoff or landing of a watched aircraft, sent to a takeoff/landing webhook (Fleet)
post.description: Signed and retried like trafficEvent. Detected in real time from the network's receivers, best effort: a takeoff or landing the network does not see is not sent. One alert per aircraft and kind every 20 minutes (circuits). A landing deduced from the aircraft disappearing near a field comes about 2.5 minutes after its last signal; if the aircraft is seen flying again within 10 minutes, flight.landing_retracted follows (same event_id), only to the webhooks that got the landing. Events detected more than 15 minutes earlier are never sent. https://flyitalyadsb.com/data/api/docs/alerts/#aircraft

airport.description: ICAO code (or the local code of a small airfield).

time.description: Unix seconds: when the network saw the aircraft at this end.

seen.description: How the airport was recognised: ground (on the ground within 6 km), low (at most 2,500 ft above it within 15 km), approach (at most 6,000 ft within 30 km, heading consistent). ground/low times are close to take-off or landing.

Flight.description: A flight observed by the network, not an airline schedule. Never the owner or operator.

duration_min.description: Observed minutes, first to last point.

day.description: UTC day the flight started; flights across midnight UTC are joined.

FlightsCoverage.description: The days searched; missing = days in the period that are not built (yet).

matched_as.description: Present when a translated form matched (e.g. a flight number).

since.description: The first UTC day not in the nightly flights yet: today, or yesterday right after midnight UTC.

error.description: Not in this plan, or briefly unavailable.

plans.description: When the plan has no today's flights: where to choose one.

TodayFlight.description: A flight of today from takeoffs and landings detected in real time: one the network does not see is missing. Repeated takeoffs and landings (circuits) are each a flight.

from.description: null: a landing with no takeoff seen since `since`.

status.description: unknown: a takeoff with no landing seen, and the aircraft is not flying now (or took off again).

duration_min.description: Landed flights with both ends: takeoff to landing.

position.description: in_flight only: where it is now.

airport.description: ICAO code where there is one, otherwise the OurAirports code.

time.description: UTC, ISO 8601 (not Unix seconds as in Flight).

near.description: true when the aircraft was more than 2 km from it: "near" the airport.

FlightEta.description: in_flight only, and only an estimate: the usual destination of the callsign in the flight history (when its usual route leaves from today's takeoff airport) and the straight-line time at the current ground speed. Absent without a usual route or under 80 knots; late while the aircraft is still climbing; never a schedule.

count.description: How many callsigns (candidates may be cut at 50).

flights.description: Flights observed on the route in the period.

usual_departure_utc.description: HH:MM, UTC: the median departure time.

aircraft.description: Up to three aircraft that flew it most.

r.description: Registration, or the ICAO address when unknown.

live.description: Present when an aircraft with this callsign is flying now.

now.description: Time of the live data, Unix seconds.

in_use.description: Runway ends with traffic now, busiest first; empty when none.

heading.description: Direction of travel on it, degrees true.

aircraft_nearby.description: Aircraft with a position within 25 km.

max_days.description: The plan's depth, in days back from today (UTC).

requested_days.description: How far back the request asked.

help.description: On 401, 403 and 429: the FAQ answer for this error.

TrafficEvent.description: An event, plus the aircraft fields known at that moment with readsb's names (flight, r, t, desc, year, alt_baro, gs, track, squawk, emergency, category, dbFlags); `source` is readsb's position type. Never the owner or operator.

time.description: When the aircraft was seen entering the cell.

distance_km.description: From the query point (or the webhook centre).

map.description: The aircraft on the live map.

for.description: aircraft: a takeoff and landing webhook for the watched aircraft, with no area.

status.description: paused-plan: the account has no paid key now.

secret.description: whsec_…, shown only in this answer.

type.description: event.emergency, event.military, event.interesting, flight.takeoff, flight.landing, flight.landing_retracted, webhook.test

last_status.description: HTTP status of the last attempt.

kind.description: any: a value that matches as a registration or a callsign.

value.description: Without separators; the ICAO address in lower case.

max.description: The plan's maximum: Fleet 25, Enterprise 250, other plans 0.

time.description: When it happened; for a landing deduced from the aircraft disappearing, its last signal.

airport.description: ICAO code where there is one, otherwise the OurAirports code.

near.description: true beyond 2 km: "near" the airport, not "at".

watch.description: The entry of the list that matched.

event_id.description: The event_id of the flight.landing it withdraws.

reason.description: reappeared: the aircraft was seen flying again.

data.description: The event (TrafficEvent, with webhook_id and distance_km from the webhook centre), or {webhook_id, message} for a test.

Aircraft.description: A record from readsb's aircraft.json. Which fields are present depends on what was received; only common ones are listed.

hex.description: ICAO address; a leading ~ marks a non-ICAO (e.g. TIS-B) address.

type.description: Source of the current position, e.g. adsb_icao, mlat, tisb_icao.

ObservedRoute.description: Only with with=route on a list: the most frequent route of the callsign in the latest 7 days of flight history. Absent when unknown. Not a schedule.

total.description: Same as count, the field name of ADSBx v2.

ac.description: The aircraft in the air now; one found by two values appears once.

not_found.description: The values with no aircraft in the air now, as written.

matched.description: Value as written -> the form found, only when they differ.

archive_unavailable.description: Present when the archive could not be listed: only recent days are included.

year.description: Year of manufacture, when the aircraft database has it.

trace_day.description: The day whose track supplied type_description and year.

live.description: When seen_now is true, also: now, callsign, source (adsb_icao, mlat, tisb_icao…) and the aircraft.json fields lat, lon, alt_baro, alt_geom, gs, track, baro_rate, squawk, emergency, category, seen, seen_pos, mlat.

now.description: Time of the live data, Unix seconds.

days_last_30.description: Days with a track among today and the previous 29 (UTC).

archive_unavailable.description: Present when the archive could not be listed: recent days only.

map.description: The public map on this aircraft: live, or its last track the map can show.

page.description: Public photo page on Planespotters.net (no image in this API).

withheld.description: Why there is no photo link.

truncated.description: More passes exist than were returned.

complete_until.description: When truncated: every pass whose closest_time is before this is listed. Ask again from here.

gaps.description: Periods NOT searched (not indexed yet, not covered, or tracks that could not be read).

passes.description: Separate times it entered the circle.

positions.description: Received positions inside the circle; 0 = interpolated between positions outside it.

history.description: The /v2/history paths of the days read.

Trace.description: readsb trace_full JSON: icao, timestamp, and trace (array of points relative to timestamp), plus aircraft metadata.
